evidence.says: LC heading is Brecher, Jeremy. Sources identify Strike! (1972) and Global village or global pillage (1998); the latter publisher CIP data sheet supplies birth year 1946, also encoded in the authority birth-date field.

Jeremy Brecher is described as a historian and documentary filmmaker. Identifiers include LC n82059590, VIAF 93206027, ISNI 0000000107923711 and Open Library OL226777A. Birth year is 1938, citing VIAF.
The graph's Open Library author is Jeremy Brecher; its identifiers explicitly link LC n82059590 and Wikidata Q19864460, with the same VIAF and ISNI. It records birth year 1938.
This author's works include Global village or global pillage, Brass Valley, Common sense for hard times and Globalization from below, matching the LC author's bibliography.

The official website linked by Wikidata lists Strike!, first published in 1972, and Global Village or Global Pillage among Brecher's books, independently connecting the item's author with LC's cited works.

Farnie and Tweedale, A Bio-Bibliography of Economic and Social History, fifth edition (2009), printed page 41, lists Brecher, Jeremy with birth year 1946 and identifies him as a coeditor of Brass Valley (1982); its entry cites Contemporary Authors Online.
IdRef instead records birth year 1938, while listing the same works, including Strike!, Global village or global pillage and Brass valley. This is a conflicting date for the same author.

notes: Same person and correct graph match. Prefer 1946 on the documentary evidence found: LC cites a publisher data sheet, corroborated by the scholarly biobibliography. The 1938 date persists in Wikidata, Open Library and IdRef, so the conflict is not fully resolved. LC HTML was inaccessible; its structured authority record was read. No replacement QID is needed.
